newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says Senate tax bill move in right direction.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says Senate tax bill move in right direction.

text.p: Senate tax-cut proposals are a step in the right direction toward implementing a budget-balancing pact but need significant modifications, said a letter made public on Thursday from Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin to Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott.

The Senate is debating tax legislation that aims to implement the requirement in the balanced-budget agreement between Congress and the Clinton administration for an $85 billion net tax cut over five years.
Rubin said the Senate bill still was "heavily-laden with special-interest provisions" and needs change.

Among sticking points, Rubin said the Clinton administration opposed transferring 4.3 cents per gallon in fuel taxes from deficit reduction to transportation trust funds because that might create pressure to spend more than planned on roads.

He also said education proposals were "insufficient and unfair to lower-income students" since there would be no general deduction for tuition expenses. Effectively, it benefits wealthy families while reducing the tax benefits to lower-income ones, Rubin said.

The Treasury Seceretary also complained that proposals to allow more generous contributions to Individual Retirement Accounts "are not sufficiently targeted" because they set no income limits for contributions to back-loaded IRAs.
The result would likely be a shift in existing savings by wealthier Americans to tax-sheltered accounts with no net increase in overall savings, Rubin said.
